title: c11 Event Envelope v2
description: Source of truth for the c11 events-stream envelope (v2). Every NDJSON line written with "v": 2 to ~/Library/Application Support/c11/events/events-<instance>.ndjson must validate against this schema. One EventEnvelope serializes to exactly one line. v2 renames the subject refs (surface → panel, pane → area), three event types (surface.created → panel.created, surface.closed → panel.closed, tab.input_sent → panel.input_sent), the metadata.changed scope values (surface → panel, pane → area), and the caller payload key (caller_tab_id / caller_surface_id → caller_panel_id; lifecycle.changed tab → panel). Logs written before v2 are never rewritten: lines with "v": 1 validate against event-envelope.v1.schema.json, and readers accept both. See Sources/Events/EventEnvelope.swift and spec/README.md.

seq.description: Monotonic per-instance sequence number, assigned on the writer's serial queue so file order and seq order always agree. The write-order oracle: consumers consume by seq, not ts. Deferred OSC title tails can follow unrelated records emitted after the last title change.

ts.description: RFC3339 / ISO-8601 UTC timestamp with fractional seconds and Z suffix, e.g. 2026-07-07T08:20:00.123Z. Captured on the emitting thread; only approximately monotonic and may invert relative to seq across racing threads or deferred OSC title tails. Approximate change-time ordering only; seq is authoritative for write order.

type.description: Dotted event type. Closed v2 taxonomy: panel.created, panel.closed, app.activated, app.deactivated, screen.locked, screen.unlocked, system.sleep, system.wake, instance.sample, workspace.created, workspace.renamed, workspace.closed, workspace.selected, workspace.switch_blocked, workspace.reordered, metadata.changed, liveness.derived, waiting.entered, waiting.left, lifecycle.changed, flag.raised, flag.lowered, flag.suppressed, flag.unsuppressed, mailbox.accepted, panel.input_sent, mailbox.delivered, conversation.resume.mode, conversation.resume.decision, hang.precursor, ask.opened, ask.closed. Stream-control markers: log.opened, log.rotated, log.dropped, log.policy, log.retention. Readers accept v1 renamed aliases. log.retention reports degraded/recovered retention coordination and does not imply dropped event coverage.

instance.description: Per-process instance id, e.g. com.stage11.c11-12345. Namespaces the sequence: seq is monotonic within one instance's log, not across instances.

v.description: Schema version. Integer, not a string. Bumps are breaking.

workspace.description: Optional. UUID string of the subject workspace this event concerns.

panel.description: Optional. UUID string of the subject panel this event concerns. (v1: surface.)

area.description: Optional. UUID string of the subject area this event concerns. (v1: pane.)

title_change_count.description: Optional on a coalesced OSC metadata.changed title tail: meaningful changes in its window, including the initial emitted change.

last_changed_at.description: Optional on a coalesced OSC metadata.changed title tail: the last meaningful title envelope's UTC timestamp, not the deferred write time.

payload.description: Optional, type-specific detail. Free-form object; any keys allowed inside. Shape is keyed by type — e.g. panel.created carries { kind, title }; metadata.changed carries { key, value, prior, source, scope } with scope panel or area; workspace.selected carries { previous?, cause, method?, caller_panel_id? }; workspace.switch_blocked carries { target, method, caller_panel_id }; workspace.reordered carries { window_id, final_workspace_ids }; lifecycle.changed carries { panel, agent, from, to, reason }; flag.raised carries { reason, caller_panel_id, by }; flag.lowered carries { by, answer?, answer_bytes?, text_recorded? } (only feed answer attaches the submitted text, and only when its original flag epoch is lowered); flag.suppressed / flag.unsuppressed carry { by }; mailbox.accepted carries { id, from, body, body_ref?, to?, topic?, reply_to?, in_reply_to?, urgent?, truncated? }; panel.input_sent carries { caller_panel_id, caller_title, target_title, kind, text, bytes, submitted, truncated?, queued? }; mailbox.delivered carries { id, recipient, via }; conversation.resume.mode carries { mode }; conversation.resume.decision carries { kind, conversation_id, mode, decision, skip_code, reason? }; hang.precursor carries { cause, culprit, count, window_ms, span_ms, durations_ms, fingerprint }; ask.opened and ask.closed carry { kind, source, source_rank, opened_at_ms, state, request_id, confirmation, blocking } and ask.closed also carries resolution (resumed, cancelled, unknown, or null). Those ask payloads never include prompt text or options. log.opened carries { pid }; log.rotated carries { rolled_to } (null when the live file was deleted and nothing rolled); log.dropped carries { count }. Readers also accept the v1 payload keys caller_tab_id, caller_surface_id, and lifecycle tab. Omitted (not encoded as null) when empty. Local history additions: presence edges may carry snapshot=true for a baseline; workspace.created carries title/root_directory, workspace.renamed title/prior, workspace.closed title; instance.sample carries rss_mb/cpu_s_total/threads and optional shutdown=true; hang.precursor adds app_active/screen_locked/rss_mb only when analytics are enabled (unknown context may be null); coalesced OSC title tails add title_change_count and last_changed_at (the latest meaningful change timestamp in RFC3339 UTC with fractional seconds, also retained in ts); log.policy carries enabled/analytics_enabled/keep_text/retention_days. Text-off panel.input_sent/mailbox.accepted carry bytes and text_recorded=false with text/body/body_ref omitted. Text-off flag.lowered omits answer and retains answer_bytes/text_recorded=false. log.retention carries state=degraded|recovered and optional reason=lock_busy|lock_unavailable. OSC title tails have a sixty-second awake deadline; input/mailbox/liveness and unrelated events retain the one-second latency contract without flushing pending tails. Non-OSC title replacements/clears at any precedence tier, description/status changes, panel/workspace close, policy changes and shutdown flush applicable tails before the boundary. Sequence numbers are write order, not title-change order. Workspace-scoped events from the temporary App.init bootstrap graph carry transient=true on every edge, including delayed callbacks and analytics-off panel edges. The installed graph remains unmarked; readers exclude marked graphs from installed-workspace replay. Classification survives recording/analytics toggle changes within the process and never fabricates closure events. Successful native terminal runtime allocation removes transient enrollment before ready callbacks, even when recording is off; a UUID with earlier marked and later unmarked events is a classification conflict that readers preserve and report.
